 THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 09.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) is filed by respondent No.2- Insurance Company challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 24.08.2016 passed in MVC No.694/2015, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.9,19,000/- due to the death of one Vijaykumar Rathod in a motor vehicle accident dated 09.09.2014.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioners that they are wife, son and mother of deceased Vijaykumar Rathod.
On 08.09.2014, at about 11.00 p.m., deceased Vijaykumar Rathod was proceeding a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-32-EC-5937 ('Motor cylce' for short) on Humnabad - Bidar road.
At Kolar-K village, industrial area, lorry bearing registration No.KA-17-A-9707 ('the offending vehicle' for short) was parked in the middle of the road, without putting on parking lights.
There were also no municipal lights or any domestic lights.
On account of the darkness, visibility was not there.
In the darkness, deceased dashed his motor cycle against the stationed lorry.
He sustained grevious injury and died on the spot.
As the wife, son and mother, petitioners were dependant on him.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally are liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: 2 5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation and income of the deceased and that petitioners were dependant on him.
They have also denied that accident occurred due to the negligent parking of the offending vehicle and that it was parked in the middle of the road without any indicators.

They have specifically pleaded that the offending vehicle was parked on the extreme left of the road with indicators and it was deceased, who was rash or negligent and without properly observing the parked lorry, he dashed the motor cycle against the offending vehicle and sustained injuries and died on the spot.
Therefore, respondents are not liable to pay the compensation and prays to reject the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. In support of petitioners claim, petitioner No. is examined as PW-1 and Exs.P-1 to P-10 are marked.
8. The driver of the offending vehicle is examined as RW-1 and Ex.R-1 is marked.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.9,19,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

The details of compensation granted by the Tribunal are as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 Loss of dependency 8,64,000  Loss of consortium 25,000  Loss of love and affection 20,000  Loss of estate 20,000  Funeral, obsequies and 10,000  transportation of dead body etc.
Petitioners as well as respondent No.1 have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

11. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the Tribunal has wholly missed itself in conceptualizing as to how the accident took place between the two vehicles and failed to appreciate the complaint averments as well as the charge sheet filed by the police.
The Tribunal has also not appreciated the fact that the petition is not maintainable for non joinder of necessary parties.
The Tribunal has also failed to appreciate that as the rider of the motor cycle, deceased was negligent.
In the light of the complaint averments and the charge sheet, the Tribunal ought to have taken into account the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
The compensation awarded is exorbitant, fanciful and without any basis and prays to allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and award.
12. Heard arguments and perused the record.

sentences.text:
The grievance of the appellant/respondent No.2 is that despite the fact that the complaint was filed by an eye witness stating that deceased was equally contributed to the cause of accident as he was riding the motor cycle in a rash or negligent manner and after conducting detailed investigation,
charge sheet is filed against both i.e., the driver of the offending vehicle as well as the deceased, the Tribunal has failed to appreciate the said fact and on flimsy grounds, gave a finding that the entire negligence was on the part of the offending vehicle in parking the offending vehicle in the middle of the road.
14. At the outset, it is relevant to note that immediately, after the accident, complaint came to be lodged by one Rajshekar Shambu, a Social Worker and Ex- President of the Gram Panchayath.
After arranging for shifting the dead body in the ambulance, he rushed to the Police Station to file the complaint at 12.00 in the midnight.

His complaint reveal that at the time of the accident,
complainant was proceeding in a motor cycle behind the motor cycle of the deceased.

The complaint states that he found the lorry parked in the middle of the road, but deceased was riding the motor cycle in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the parked lorry.
Had he been little careful and was at a reasonable speed, he could have avoided the accident.
Ex.P-8 is the sketch of the place of incident, which goes to show that though the lorry was parked in the left side of the road, there was still sufficient space on the right side.
Had the deceased was little careful, he would have avoided the parked lorry and stirred on the right side of the road and proceeded further.

15. After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned Police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as well as the deceased stating that while the driver of the offending vehicle was guilty of parking the vehicle not on the extreme left side of the road but in the middle of the road, deceased was equally negligent in riding his motor cycle in a rash or negligent manner and dashing against the parked lorry.

When all these factors are considered, it would lead to an irresistible conclusion that while the driver of the offending vehicle has negligently parked the vehicle, deceased was also negligent and he was riding the motor cycle in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner.
Therefore, it is necessary to attribute some portion of the negligence on the part of deceased and deduct that portion of the compensation.

16. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances and the entire evidence placed on record,
this Court is of the considered opinion that attributing 10% of the negligence to the deceased would meet the ends of justice.

Therefore, out of total compensation, petitioners are entitled for only 90%
of the compensation and remaining 10% is being deducted towards the negligence attributed to the deceased.

17. In the result, appeal deserves to be allowed in part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal filed by respondent No.2/Insurance Company is allowed in part.
